brief: Goldman's Coppersmith argues next week's AI news matters more for US stocks than the inflation data, with the SPX straddle for the coming week at roughly 1 percent. The macro chain: the firm's Risk Appetite Indicator has its growth component near the top of its post-COVID range while the monetary policy component stays negative, so further gains in risk appetite need lower rates rather than stronger growth, and embedded growth optimism leaves less room for growth or geopolitical disappointment. On the micro side, Tech-led earnings supported by AI capex draw lower multiples as leverage rises across the AI ecosystem and higher long-end yields pressure valuations outside Tech, so the strategy team expects lower equity Sharpe ratios. Positioning is the offset. Prime brokerage gross leverage for US fundamental long/shorts sits in the 27th percentile and net leverage in the 4th, semis vol proxy VXSMH has fallen from roughly 65 in July to 36, and put-call skew stays flat, so Coppersmith favours owning right-tail expressions through options into the Communacopia conference. Hedging runs through downside on the SPX ex-AI index or long Broad AI versus short SPXXAI. Brazil's RSI is 76 and a runoff poll shows Bolsonaro 45 to Lula 44.
